label: digit 3 input at original positions 4-7 in sequences starting with s/z/f that contain v/t/g
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.001% of steps). It fires only during the original phase, nearly always (98.5% of mass) when the input is the digit 3, at original positions 4-7 (peaking at t=5). Activation also depends on the prefix: the first token is s (68% of mass), z (21%) or f (10%), and earlier inputs usually include v, t, g or u. The strongest activations are on 3 at t=5 after prefixes like s z v c u or s r t v u. It never fires in the delimiter or copy phase, at t<4, or on other tokens (apart from a few weak exceptions on y/e/z). The predicate covers 91% of activation mass on dev, but precision is only about 5%: most 3s in such contexts stay inactive, so the conjunction that actually triggers it (probably a specific hidden-state direction) is only roughly captured.
